title: Espressioni di Tempo e Avverbi di Frequenza
subtitle: Sempre, spesso, a volte, raramente, mai — and where they go in the sentence.
objectives: Use the core frequency adverbs from most to least frequent
Place frequency adverbs correctly in simple and compound tenses

content.intro: Frequency adverbs let you describe routines and habits with precision — and they follow a placement rule that differs from the present tense to the passato prossimo.
content.explanation: In the present tense, frequency adverbs usually follow the verb directly: Vado sempre in palestra. In the passato prossimo, short, common adverbs (sempre, già, mai, ancora, ma also ben-known più) slot in between the auxiliary and the past participle: Non sono mai stato a Venezia.

rules.heading: a) Frequency scale, most to least
b) Mai — "never" needs non
rules.body: Non before the verb + mai after (or between auxiliary and participle): Non mangio mai carne. (I never eat meat.) Non ho mai visto quel film. (I've never seen that film.)

rules.heading: c) Placement in the passato prossimo
rules.body: Sempre, mai, già, ancora, più typically go between the auxiliary and the participle: Ho già mangiato. Non ho ancora finito. (I've already eaten. I haven't finished yet.)

examples.en: I always have breakfast at eight.

examples.it: Vado spesso in palestra dopo il lavoro.
examples.en: I often go to the gym after work.

examples.it: Non sono mai stata in Giappone.
A volte lavoro anche il weekend.
examples.en: Sometimes I even work on the weekend.

commonMistakes.why: Mai needs non before the verb — Italian, unlike English "never", still requires the negative particle.
Same rule in the passato prossimo — non is required alongside mai.
Già typically sits between the auxiliary and the participle, not after the whole verb phrase.

items.explanation: Mai needs non before the verb.
Già slots between auxiliary and participle.

items.prompt: Which word means the LEAST frequent (besides never)?
items.explanation: Raramente (rarely) is the least frequent option here, short of mai (never).

answer: Non sono mai stato a Roma.
items.explanation: Mai requires non before the verb.

summary: Frequency scale: sempre > di solito > spesso > a volte > raramente > non ... mai.
Mai (never) always needs non before the verb — Italian double-marks the negation.
In the passato prossimo, sempre/mai/già/ancora typically go between the auxiliary and the participle.
